headline: San Antonio wears silver and black every day, and Fiesta color on the days that count.
thesis: San Antonio is a one-team city, and silver and black is its civic dress. West Side abuelas wear it, and so do East Side families who remember the Iceman, Joint Base San Antonio households and Laredo road-trippers. Color is for occasions: Fiesta's pink, turquoise and marigold, the medal pins, conjunto and the West Side's sign-painted shopfronts. Fans guard the Duncan-Popovich habit of restraint, so keep core product monochrome and precise. Spend color only on occasions the city already keeps: the returning Fiesta-stripe City Edition, an April Fiesta drop, Cup Fridays and the Rodeo Road Trip. Make every cultural piece with credited, paid local artists from the West Side and the East Side. The money is in price tiers for a price-aware, bilingual region that shops for whole families, led by an always-on Wembanyama youth ladder.

archetype.name: The Civic Family Contender
archetype.description: A multigenerational, Latino-majority, military-heavy fan base that spans the West, East and South Sides. It treats the Spurs as the city's shared family table and prizes humility over flash. After losing the 2026 Finals, it now expects a title.

pulse.teamMoment: The Spurs won the West in 2026 at 62-20, beating OKC 4-3 in the West finals, then lost the Finals 4-1 to the Knicks. They extended Wembanyama (5 years, $252M) and Fox through 2029-30. The core runs it back under Mitch Johnson, and they're title co-favorites with OKC. Opening night, Oct 20, is the West finals rematch with OKC. The Knicks come back on Christmas Day at MSG and on Mar 7 in San Antonio.
pulse.sentiment: Confident and hungry, not celebratory. Fans are proud of the West title, stung by the Knicks and protective of Spurs humility. They watch Project Marvel and the Frost Bank Center lease talks with civic interest, not alarm.

topInsights.title: Fiesta is the city's design system, and it lands on the first round
topInsights.insight: Fiesta's ten days in the second half of April overlap the first playoff round: Battle of Flowers, Fiesta Flambeau, NIOSA at La Villita. Thanks to its medal culture, locals already treat a hat or sash as a surface for collectible pins. Fans embraced the Fiesta-stripe City Edition because it turns that palette into stripes on black instead of costume.
topInsights.implication: Make April the market's biggest product moment. Pre-announce one Fiesta capsule and a four-medal set built to be worn at Fiesta events. Make them with local medal makers, and clear them with every Fiesta organization whose name or medal design appears.

topInsights.title: Restraint is the brand; color is the occasion
topInsights.insight: Thirty years of silver, black and white under Duncan and Popovich made understatement a civic value. Spurs gear gets worn every month, not just on game nights. The warmest nostalgia belongs to the teal, orange and fuchsia Fiesta era of 1989-2002, but fans want it as an accent on black, not a takeover.
topInsights.implication: Keep core product tonal and monochrome, with small, precise local details like woven labels and bilingual hang tags. Save loud color for City Edition, Fiesta and capsule drops.

topInsights.title: The hand-made West Side has never led a Spurs uniform
topInsights.insight: San Antonio's own craft is conjunto, the button accordion and bajo sexto that the Guadalupe's Tejano Conjunto Festival has championed for four decades. It's also Fiesta medals, made by hundreds of local organizations, and the hand-painted letters on West Side taquerias, panaderias and tire shops. Heritage nights have nodded to it. None of it has led a Spurs City Edition the way the Fiesta stripe has.
topInsights.implication: Commission named local letterers, printmakers and conjunto musicians for credited graphics now. Pitch a West Side City Edition concept for 2027-28, but only after Nike and the NBA confirm the design lock date.

topInsights.title: The East Side is the arena's neighborhood and the franchise's root
topInsights.insight: Frost Bank Center sits on the East Side, the historic heart of Black San Antonio. The fan lineage starts with George Gervin's Iceman finger-roll at HemisFair Arena and runs through David Robinson, Sean Elliott and Avery Johnson. Each January the city's MLK March, one of the largest in the country, walks through the same neighborhood. Project Marvel's planned downtown move makes the East Side's tie to the team a live question.
topInsights.implication: Add an East Side thread with its own credited Black San Antonio designers and institutions. Start with a Gervin-era heritage capsule (with Gervin's agreement) and a Black History Month and MLK week moment. Put the community first, and never let it read as a farewell to the neighborhood.

topInsights.title: Taste is set on the West Side; volume runs through malls and Academy
topInsights.insight: Cultural credibility comes from the West Side, Market Square and the Southtown and Blue Star scene. Volume flows through North Star, La Cantera, Ingram Park and South Park mall chains, Academy, Dick's and the Frost Bank Center team store. Independent sneaker culture is thinner than in Houston or Dallas.
topInsights.implication: Seed artist drops first in community pop-ups: the Guadalupe, First Fridays, Ingram Park. Then scale the stripe and core product at the volume doors through allocation and shop-in-shop quality. Don't build a flagship.

topInsights.title: Tier for the family of four, the E-5 and the Alamo Heights collector
topInsights.insight: This is a price-aware market. Spending clusters on the Texas August sales-tax holiday (items under $100), military 1st-and-15th paydays, Christmas and Las Posadas, and Fiesta. Flea markets like Traders Village set a bootleg price floor. And Wembanyama is now the role model for a generation of local kids.
topInsights.implication: Run the price ladder all year. Push a sub-$100 youth and tee tier for the holidays now, and peak it at the August tax holiday. Make the swingman the committed buy, and protect authentic and limited drops. Never chase flea-market prices with the top tier.

topInsights.title: Spurs Nation is a region, a border and now a global audience
topInsights.insight: The fan base runs to Laredo, Corpus Christi, the Rio Grande Valley and Monterrey. Mexican shoppers drive to La Cantera, North Star and the San Marcos outlets around Buen Fin and the December holidays. Ginobili's Latin American following and Wembanyama's French one, plus games in Austin, Paris and Manchester, make this a team that travels.
topInsights.implication: Make bilingual, Spanish-first copy the default on local drops, and time November promos to Buen Fin. Run an Austin game-week pop-up for the I-35 corridor. Give the international games a clean silver-and-black travel story.

opportunities.title: Hecho a Mano: West Side artist and conjunto series
opportunities.summary: Small, credited, paid drops led by the Guadalupe Cultural Arts Center and conjunto musicians, with San Antonio printmakers and letterers. They earn the credibility mass product can't buy.

Set paid commissions plus a royalty with Nike legal before outreach. Widen the roster through a Guadalupe open call for younger and women printmakers, with Piñata Protest as the younger-scene complement. Any Flaco Jiménez tribute is a licensing conversation with his family, never a likeness on a tee.

collection.name: Puro SA
collection.story: San Antonio dresses in silver and black every day and in Fiesta color when the city celebrates. Puro SA keeps the two apart. There's a precise monochrome core and a Fiesta season that layers like medals. Heritage lines come from the city's own makers, from the West Side's conjunto and sign-painted streets to the East Side's Iceman years.

uniform.narrative: Start the pitch now for the first new City Edition after the Fiesta stripe, likely 2027-28, but only once Nike and the NBA confirm the design lock date. It draws on what only San Antonio has. A commissioned local sign painter draws original letterforms from named West Side shop signs. The conjunto accordion sets the structural pattern, and Fiesta-medal ribbons set the colors. The warm-up, shooting shirt, cap and tee can prove the look this season without uniform approval.

risks.risk: The 2027-28 City Edition design window may already be closing. The Rótulo concept also needs NBA and Spurs approval for numerals, wordmark and court.
risks.mitigation: Ask Nike Basketball Apparel and the NBA for the real lock date first. Prove the look through warm-ups, caps and tees that need no uniform approval.

risks.risk: Many local organizations hold Fiesta names and medals, and Selena, Flaco Jiménez, H-E-B and Whataburger are tightly licensed. Lifting Mexican-American, Black or Indigenous culture would read as appropriation: real shop signs, mission architecture, Dia de los Muertos imagery, the Alamo.
risks.mitigation: Clear each rights holder before design lock, and keep likenesses to estate-licensed conversations. Commission, credit and pay artists from each community, and run designs past the Guadalupe, East Side partners and the Tap Pilam Coahuiltecan Nation.

risks.risk: The Finals loss makes Dec 25 and Mar 7 product a sore spot, and a playoff exit could sour the April drop.
risks.mitigation: No Knicks-baiting graphics and no title or Finals language. Sell Fiesta as a city moment, and hold champion product until it's earned.

risks.risk: A popular returning City Edition invites counterfeits and Traders Village bootlegs. Named-player product can also clash with the affiliations of Wembanyama, Fox, Castle and Harper.
risks.mitigation: Win the entry price with a real sub-$100 tier. Keep stripe product in stock and coordinate takedowns with the league. Run a player-affiliation check before any named-player product.

risks.risk: Project Marvel and lease politics make arena, downtown and East Side framing sensitive.
risks.mitigation: Keep skyline and arena-move imagery off product. Frame East Side work as the neighborhood's team, not a farewell.

scorecard.rationale: Opportunity, culture and fandom run well above average. The Spurs are title co-favorites led by Wembanyama, in a one-team region that runs to Mexico. They have some of the league's most specific design material: Fiesta, conjunto, West Side craft and the East Side's Iceman lineage. Retail is ordinary: mall, Academy and arena-store volume in a price-aware market, with a thin independent sneaker scene and a real bootleg channel.
